name: Milk collection centres and chillers
shape_facts: Role: independent collector/chiller owner, agent for a processor, cooperative, or a farm’s own collection point.
Volume handled per day and number of suppliers (farmers, dodhis).
Testing done at intake: fat, SNF, lactometer, adulteration strips, nothing.
Who buys the milk: processor, city gawalas, shops, dahi/sweet makers.
Payment cycles to suppliers and from buyers (daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly).
Cooling and power: chiller capacity, generator, solar; frequency of outages.
Transport: own tankers/vehicles, hired, buyer collects.
scope_rule: pi notes the business side of collecting, testing, chilling and selling milk: intake records, supplier payments, quality disputes, buyer rejections, cash and advances, power and transport, staff and records. pi does not advise on testing methods to “pass” a sample, preservatives, chemicals, or milk-quality standards, and never helps disguise adulteration or tamper with tests or tankers. It does not give food-authority licensing or tax advice. It records farmers, dodhis and drivers by role and count, never names, CNICs, phone numbers or bank details.

vocabulary.fat / SNF: butterfat and solids-not-fat, used to price milk
vocabulary.lactometer: instrument used to check milk density
vocabulary.dodhi: collector who brings milk from farms, often on a motorbike with cans

problems.phrase: Fat readings are written by hand and farmers argue every payday
Suppliers say our test is wrong and move to another chiller
Some dodhis add water and we only find out at the plant
Plant rejected a whole tanker and deducted it from our payment
Litres collected don’t match litres dispatched
Advances to farmers aren’t tracked properly, some never repay
We pay suppliers weekly but the plant pays us monthly
Cash payments to 300 farmers on one day is a risk
Generator broke and milk in the chiller turned
Diesel cost for generator and tankers is unknown per litre
Tanker reaches the plant late and gets penalised
Driver may be skimming milk on the way
Flush season we get more milk than we can sell
Summer supply drops and the plant still wants volume
Competing collectors poach suppliers with a better rate
Testing staff can be pressured or bribed by suppliers
Payment slips are handwritten, farmers lose them
End-of-week supplier statements take my staff two days
Can’t see daily intake across my 5 centres
Chiller cleaning gets skipped
Food authority licence and hygiene paperwork overwhelms us
Want to add a new route but don’t know if it pays

setup: Roughly how much milk do you collect a day?
From how many farmers or dodhis ?
disputes: How often do suppliers argue about fat or rate?
buyers: How often do they reject or deduct?
volume: Does the volume collected match what you dispatch?
Where do you think the gap is?
payments: How often do you pay suppliers, and how often are you paid?
How are payouts made — cash or transfer?
advances: Do you give advances to farmers?
power: How often does the chiller lose power?
transport: How do you know when it leaves and arrives?
multi-centre: How do you see each centre’s intake daily?
growth: What would you need to know before adding a route?

seasons: - Pakistan: flush season in winter and spring brings surplus milk and lower prices; lean season in summer (May–August) brings shortages, higher prices and intense competition for suppliers. - Ramadan raises demand for milk, dahi and dairy sweets; Eid ul Fitr spikes sweet-shop demand. - Eid ul Adha disrupts supply (animals sold, staff away) for a week or more. - Monsoon roads and floods disrupt routes; heatwaves strain chillers and generators. - UAE: farm-based collection is smaller; summer heat and Ramadan dominate. - Canada: milk is supply-managed and collected by provincial boards; independent collection is limited, so this pack is mainly PK/UAE.
care: Never helps mask adulteration, add preservatives, tamper with tests, readings or tankers, or “pass” a quality check; declines plainly.
No advice on testing standards, chemicals or food-authority rules beyond noting the admin effort.
Bribery of testing staff: pi notes it as an integrity problem and does not engage in arranging or hiding it.
Large cash payouts and robbery risk; if a robbery just happened or someone is in danger, pi points to 15/1122.
Electrical, ammonia/refrigerant or tanker accidents: emergency services first.
Farmer data: roles and counts only; no names, CNIC, phone or bank numbers.
build_ideas: Intake app at the centre: supplier code, litres, fat/SNF readings entered or pulled from an existing analyser, timestamp.
Instant WhatsApp or SMS slip to each supplier after each delivery with litres, readings and amount.
Weekly/fortnightly supplier statements generated automatically with advances deducted.
Advance ledger per supplier with repayment schedule.
Dispatch log per tanker: litres loaded, seal photo, departure and arrival times, plant receipt and any rejection.
Collected vs dispatched reconciliation by day and centre.
Buyer ledger with deductions, rejections and payments.
Multi-centre owner dashboard: litres, average fat, suppliers active, cash due in and out.
Generator and chiller log with downtime and diesel use.
Cleaning and hygiene checklist with photo proof.
Route profitability view from the business’s own volumes and costs.

exchange.text: Hamara chiller hai Okara ke paas, roz 6,000 litre ikattha hota hai. Har hafte payment pe farmers se jhagra hota hai.
Har hafte ka jhagra thaka deta hai. Jhagra zyada tar fat ki reading pe hota hai ya rate pe?
Fat pe, kehte hain hum kam likhte hain.
Noted — farmers fat ki reading pe shak karte hain. Reading abhi kahan likhi jati hai, aur farmer ko kya milta hai?
Register mein, farmer ko kuch nahi milta, bas hafte ke baad paise.
Noted, farmer ko har delivery ki koi parchi nahi milti. Aap suppliers ko payment cash mein karte hain ya transfer?
